Subject: Exhibit H harmonization + automatic rate trigger clarification

Hi Marta / Oliver —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a proposed update to the Order Form (Exhibit H) that harmonizes two throughput SKUs into a single line and clarifies the automatic rate trigger that applies when aggregate monthly consumption exceeds the threshold for a sustained period. High level changes (see attached Solaritiy_SOW_v2.docx):

- Consolidated SKUs: simplifies billing and reduces invoice churn.
- Rate trigger: when average monthly tokens > 1.2B over a 90-day rolling window, the per-token rate transitions to the next published tier automatically.
- Safety controls: notification goes to the purchaser, and we propose a 30-day notice before new rates appear on invoices.

We want to avoid back-and-forth redlines. Could you please confirm if this form is acceptable to your procurement/legal teams or flag the specific clauses you want us to revise?

Attachments: Solaritiy_SOW_v2.docx (draft), redlines_20280501.pdf (previous internal redline).

Proposed next steps: if acceptable, we'll prepare an updated DocuSign envelope and route to your signer; if not, please return your redlines and we can schedule a legal 30-min sync.

Thanks,

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clean draft. A couple items Procurement & Legal flagged on first read (attached redlines_20280503.pdf):

- Automatic rate increases: our counsel is uncomfortable with a fully automatic price step without an explicit approval path.
- Notification timing: 30 days is short for internal budgeting and PO updates; can we get 60 days?
- Cap: need a guardrail on how much the rate can move in any 90-day window (Solarity requests a 15% cap).

We want to get to signature this month; can you propose a compromise? If you have a version with tracked changes we can review faster.

Best,

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Exhibit H harmonization + automatic rate trigger clarification

Karthik / Ben — forwarding Solarity's redlines. Quick analysis:

- Legal ask (no auto without approval) is standard negotiation posture. We can accept automation if we bake in layered protections. Proposed options:

Option A (manual gate): keep trigger but require written approval from Solarity procurement before new tier applies; 60-day notice; no cap change beyond contracted ladder.

Option B (auto + protections): automatic tiering remains; Redwood provides 60-day advance notice, a 15% per-quarter max increase cap, and a one-time transitional credit equal to 10% of the first month of new tier (or $15,000 min), to soften budget shock.

Operational note: Option B preserves our self-service billing model (preferred) and reduces churn for both sides. If you want, Ben can run a quick P&L sensitivity on Option B impact for the first 12 months.

Suggest we propose Option B and see if Solarity will accept the compromise. If they insist on manual gate, expect slower turnaround.

Laura
VP, Commercial — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@solarity.com>, Oliver Chan <oliver.chan@solarity.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, procurement@solarity.com
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit H harmonization + automatic rate trigger clarification

Marta — thanks for the quick read and the redlines. After internal discussion we can agree to a middle path that aims to address procurement concerns while keeping the automated model intact. Proposed compromise (pulled into updated draft attached and DocuSign ready):

- Notice: Redwood will provide a 60-day written notice prior to applying the higher rate to invoices.
- Cap: rate increases triggered by the Exhibit H ladder will be limited to a 15% maximum change to the per-token rate over any 90-day window.
- Transitional credit: if the trigger occurs within the first 12 months of the Order Form effective date, Redwood will apply a one-time invoice credit of $15,000 to the month following the new tier taking effect.
- Exception path: either party can request a procurement call within the 60-day window; if both parties agree, the billing change can be paused for a single 30-day extension while remediation is worked out.

I've attached an updated draft (Solarity_SOW_v2.docx) with the language changed and a DocuSign envelope link ready: https://docusign.net/rdw/RD-4821-exhibitH-dslink. If this looks acceptable, please confirm and we'll send the DocuSign envelope to your signer.

If you prefer a tracked-changes PDF we can generate that as well — Ben, can you produce the P&L sensitivity and a short note on how the 15% cap affects our quarterly revenue projection?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
